messages:
alex-support: Customer reported production failures for function/tool calls on /v1/respond. High-level: their agent sends a JSON payload with tools list, and our router picked the wrong tool intermittently, causing crashes and 500s. Customer: corp-acme (acct: acct_5421). Region: us-west-2. Impact: 30% of calls failing for last 20m.

rita-se: can you paste any example requests?

alex-support: yes. sending sanitized sample and logs.

alex-support: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/respond \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "input": "Find nearest parking garage",
    "tools": [
      {"name": "geo.lookup", "schema": {"type":"object","properties":{"lat":{"type":"number"},"lon":{"type":"number"}}}},
      {"name": "parking.reserve", "schema": {"type":"object","properties":{"parkId":{"type":"string"},"duration":{"type":"integer"}}}},
      {"name": "place.search", "schema": {"type":"object","properties":{"query":{"type":"string"}}}}
    ],
    "tool_args": {"placeId":"abcd1234","lat":37.77,"lon":-122.41}
  }'```

alex-support: logs show router selected `geo.lookup` but payload matched `parking.reserve` (customer sends `placeId` which should map to parking.reserve).

jamie-oncall: curious — router selects based on heuristics + top-level keys if no explicit `tool_name` right?

luis-eng: yes, current selection flow: 1) if model returns `tool_name` use it, 2) else fallback to schema matching by looking up top-level keys vs tool schemas in order, 3) tie-breaker uses model intent score. There was a recent micro-optimization that short-circuits on first schema partial-match to speed up cold-path routing.

mike-ml: that short-circuit was deployed in canary last week (2026-02-18). Could be regressing cases where arg names overlap across tool schemas.

rita-se: reproduction steps I ran (local, same customer shape):
```bash
# reproduce locally
curl -s -X POST http://staging-router.local/respond \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"tools":[{"name":"geo.lookup","schema":{"properties":{"lat":{},"lon":{}}}},{"name":"parking.reserve","schema":{"properties":{"parkId":{},"duration":{}}}},{"name":"place.search","schema":{"properties":{"query":{}}}}],"tool_args":{"placeId":"abcd1234","lat":37.77,"lon":-122.41}}' | jq
```

rita-se: when I run that against current prod router code I get:
```json
{"selected_tool":"geo.lookup","match_score":0.48,"matched_keys":["lat","lon"]}
```

rita-se: but customer payload clearly intends parking.reserve (placeId). The problem is ordering: `tool_args` lists `placeId` after other keys, and our partial-match logic picks first schema that reaches threshold, ignoring presence of stronger evidence later in payload.

jamie-oncall: can we hotfix router to compute full match scores across all tools instead of short-circuiting? Even a quick fix that checks presence of unique keys (like `parkId` or `placeId`) should mitigate.

luis-eng: quick mitigation: tweak tie-breaker so that presence of any tool-specific key with high uniqueness weight overrides partial-match short-circuit. I'll push a patch to staging and can roll to prod if tests pass.

deploy-bot: deploy requested by luis-eng: deploy/router-match-fix -> staging (pipeline #4823) :rocket:

mike-ml: also noticed model sometimes emits an implicit `intent` string. We should prefer an explicit `tool_name` field from the model if present. But this is separate.

alex-support: customer asks for immediate mitigation — can we add a per-customer mapping so their requests always route parking-related args to parking.reserve?

rita-se: yes, we have customer-specific routing overrides in the console. I added a temporary rule for acct_5421 to map `placeId` and `parkId` keys to `parking.reserve`. That should reduce failures immediately.

alex-support: thanks. monitoring now shows failures drop from 30% -> 6% in 8m. still seeing a few spikes.

luis-eng: pushing a full fix to prod in 20 minutes. Patch summary: compute full-key match vector across tool schemas, then score with uniqueness weights; remove early-exit in short-circuit path. Adding unit tests for overlapping-key edgecases.

mike-ml: please add regression test using the exact customer sample payload so we don't slip again.

luis-eng: will do. tagging @mike-ml on the PR.

jamie-oncall: after prod deploy, monitor the error-rate for acct_5421 and the global tool-selection mismatch metric (router.mismatch.rate). If it doesn't improve roll back.

deploy-bot: deploy completed: prod/router-match-fix #4823 -> prod (user: luis-eng) :white_check_mark: (1765550360)

rita-se: post-deploy check: acct_5421 failures -> 0.8% now, routing mismatch metric down 92%.

alex-support: customer notified and happy with the temporary mapping + our fix. They asked for post-mortem and timeline.

luis-eng: I'll draft a short postmortem: root cause = short-circuit schema matching optimization + overlapping arg names; mitigation = per-customer override + scoring fix; followups = add unit/regression tests, add analytics to detect similar overlapped schemas, consider encouraging explicit `tool_name` from model.

mike-ml: also let's add documentation note in API reference about ambiguous tool argument shapes and best-practices for customers (prefer explicit `tool_name` or unique key names).

alex-support: filing INC-2026-115 for tracking + will CC customer. Closing thread once PMM has postmortem. Thanks all :pray:
